title: R_4(5(x-y)=3z) = 625
statement: The 4-colour Rado number of the equation 5(x-y) = 3z is exactly 625: every 4-colouring of {1,...,625} contains a monochromatic solution, and some 4-colouring of {1,...,624} avoids one.

provenance.conjectured_by: construction + literature: Chang-De Loera-Wesley Lemma 4.1 gives R_k >= a^k for gcd(a,b)=1 by the a-adic valuation colouring, and their Theorem 1.2(3) gives equality at k=3 for a >= b+2. b=3 is the LAST cell at a=5,k=4 still inside that hypothesis (5 >= 3+2 exactly), so a^4 = 625 was the prediction; b=4 lies outside it and breaks to 741.
searched_by: axeyum native proof-producing CDCL on host s4, run as a memory-bounded transient systemd --user service (MemoryHigh=70G/MemoryMax=90G): 220,077,720 steps, 19,877,980,843 bytes of DRAT, solve 8,762.2 s

A first attempt on s0 was destroyed at 2h15m when systemd-oomd killed the entire session cgroup under memory pressure (68.36% > 50.00% for >20s, 27 processes, 83.6 GB peak). Not a kernel OOM; it kills by cgroup, so nohup is irrelevant. The re-run was isolated on an idle host and peaked well inside its throttle.
NO external solver was used anywhere in this claim (ADR-0002)
checked_by: check_drat_backward (ADR-0382) in the same process, 14,499.6 s -- CHECKING COST MORE THAN SEARCHING (4h02m against 2h26m)

the lower-bound colouring re-verified from its stored file three ways: the construction, the encoder's own first_monochromatic, and the family's brute-force enumerator, which shares no code with the encoder

provenance.machine: solved on linux x86-64, 4 cores, 61 GiB (s1); proof moved and checked on linux x86-64, 16 cores, 123 GiB (s4)

prior_art.citation: Y. Chang, J. A. De Loera, W. J. Wesley, 'Rado Numbers and SAT Computations', ISSAC 2022 / arXiv:2210.03262
prior_art.establishes: NEW. Table 10 of arXiv:2210.03262 is the only published four-colour table for this family: 20 cells, 13 populated (12 exact plus the bare '> 225' at (2,3)), 7 blank. (5,2) is one of the blanks. Census read from the rendered v1 PDF cell by cell and cross-checked against this repository's ledger over all 25 k=3 cells and all 12 exact k=4 cells with zero disagreements, so the blank is a real blank and not a transcription slip. OEIS full-text search for 'Rado number' returns 7 sequences, none for this family at k >= 3 colours.

evidence.supports: the exact CNF the refutation decided, so the verdict names a formula
evidence.checker_command: cargo run --release -q -p axeyum-search --example rado_dump_cnf -- a=5 b=3 k=4 n=625 out=/tmp/F_625.cnf
evidence.notes: Pinned by REGENERATION: the bytes must come back out of the same encoder.

evidence.supports: R_4(5(x-y)=3z) > 624: the a-adic valuation colouring of [1,624] has no monochromatic solution
evidence.notes: Verified three ways: the construction, the encoder's own first_monochromatic, and the family's brute-force enumerator, which shares no code with the encoder. NOTE: this file is byte-identical to the b=2 cell's witness, which is correct and not a copy -- the a-adic valuation colouring of Lemma 4.1 depends on a and k only, never on b, so one colouring witnesses the lower bound across the whole a=5,k=4 row.

evidence.supports: R_4(5(x-y)=3z) <= 625: no 4-colouring of [1,625] avoids a monochromatic solution
